method: Static reading of the IDA Pro listing in the public disassembly repository. No ROM file was downloaded or analysed; every address below is the CPU address printed by IDA in that listing.
addressSpaces: The listing uses 68000 CPU addresses (ROM window starts at $000000). File offsets in the ROM header equal CPU addresses for REV 00 because the cartridge maps at $000000, but this project did not verify that mapping against a ROM.

records.claim: Player walk speed is read from a per-character byte table indexed by ObjMode, then converted to 16.16 fixed point by ext.w + swap + asr.l #4.
records.location: Update_Inertia subroutine, listing line 6656; table byte_3670 at line 6696
records.evidence: move.b (a1,d1.w),d2 ; ext.w d2 ; swap d2 ; asr.l #4,d2 ; move.l d2,X_Inertia(a0). Table entry 5 ($30) therefore becomes $30<<16>>4 = $30000 = 3.0 px/tick.
records.confidence: verified-arithmetic, value inferred from table layout
records.uncertainty: The table was not matched byte-for-byte against a running ROM; the mapping of table index -> animation/mode was inferred from ObjMode values and the identical 5-entry pattern repeated per character.

records.claim: Depth-axis movement uses a second velocity byte in the same table pair at 4x the horizontal step (3.0 -> 12.0 px/tick).
records.location: byte_3670 entry 5 = $30, next byte = $C0; Update_Inertia reads 1(a1,d1.w) into Y_Inertia
records.evidence: $C0 converted the same way = 12.0 px/tick. SoR1 runs at 60 fps so 12 px/tick is fast enough to cross the lane in a few ticks.
records.uncertainty: This project did not confirm that both bytes are used simultaneously in one frame (the code clears one inertia when the other is set via the bclr #2,$58(a0) path).

records.claim: Jump initial velocity is -7.0 px/tick and gravity is 0.90625 px/tick^2.
records.location: loc_20BA jump start (listing line 3860: move.l #$FFF90000,Jump_Inertia(a0)); sub_389A gravity (line 6872: move.l #$E800,d0 ; add.l d0,Jump_Inertia(a0)); sub_3886 velocity clamp (line 6849: cmpi.l #$C0000,$24(a0))
records.evidence: $FFF90000 as 16.16 = -7.0. $E800 as 16.16 = 0.90625. The clamp caps downward speed at $C0000 = 12.0 px/tick.
records.uncertainty: None for the constants; frame-to-frame application order (gravity before or after position) was not traced in full.

records.claim: A single player attack can only damage one object: the active attack box is sized 40x32 px (X+0x28, Y+0x20) around the attacker offset by (-0x14, -0x10).
records.evidence: move.w XPos(a0),d1 ; addi.w #-$14,d1 ; move.w d1,d2 ; addi.w #$28,d2 ... addi.w #-$10,d3 ; move.w d3,d4 ; addi.w #$20,d4 ... it then tests enemy SST fields XPos/YPos/field $18 (a depth-like value offset by ±8).
records.uncertainty: The loop bound ($43 = 67 entries) and the exact meaning of SST field $18 are inferred; the routine name Chk_Hit is the disassembly author's, not Capcom/Sega's.

records.claim: Depth tolerance against enemies is +-8 units in the collision test.
records.location: Chk_Hit, line 6022-6026: move.w $18(a0),d5 ; addi.w #-8,d5 ; move.w d5,d6 ; addq.w #8,d6
records.evidence: The comparison window around the attacker's depth value is [-8, +8].
records.uncertainty: It is unclear whether $18 is the same axis as YPos (screen Y) or a separate depth value; the two are separate SST fields, which suggests a 3D-ish layout.

records.claim: Object state is a table of word-sized handlers indexed by ObjMode, with 2 consecutive modes per state.
records.evidence: Modes 0/1 Init_Stand, 2/3 Obj_Stand, 4/5 Obj_Player_Pose, 6..F Obj_Player_Walk, 10/11 Obj_Jump_1, 12/13 Obj_Jump_2, 14/15 Obj_Jump_Land, 16/17 Obj_Jump_Attack, 18..1D Obj_Attack, 1E/1F Obj_Attack_KO, 22/23 Obj_BackAttack_1, 24/25 Obj_BackAttack_2, 56..59 death, 5A/5B Obj_Player_Hit, 5C/5D Obj_Player_KO, 5E Obj_Player_GetUp.
records.uncertainty: Modes above 5E were not enumerated in this pass.

records.claim: Attack damage is applied by Chk_Attack_Player, which negates a damage byte, calls Update_HealthBar and returns a flag when health reaches 0.
records.evidence: move.b AtkDamage(a1),d7 ... neg.w d7 ; jsr Update_HealthBar ; tst.w Health(a0) ; bmi/beq -> return -1.
records.uncertainty: Actual per-attack damage values live in each character's animation data and were not extracted here.

records.claim: Frame timing is per-object: FrameTimer(a0) counts down, and the animation advances when it reaches zero.
records.location: Obj_Stand / Obj_Player_Walk / Update_Frame, listing lines 3690-3700 and 7019
records.evidence: Obj_Stand: subq.b #1,FrameTimer(a0) ; bne.w Chk_ButtonPress. Obj_Player_Walk calls Update_Inertia then Update_Frame every tick.
records.uncertainty: The per-animation table that sets FrameTimer was not located in this pass.

records.claim: The disassembly repository contains four IDA .idb databases and four text listings, covering SoR1 (JUE) (REV 00), SoR2 (U), SoR3 (U) and Bare Knuckle 3 (J).
records.location: Assemblies/ and IDA Pro Databases/ directories
records.evidence: Directory listing from the cloned repository; the SoR1 listing carries the IDA header 'Input MD5 : 569CFEC15813294A8F0CF88CCCC8C151, CRC32 : BFF227C6'.
records.uncertainty: The .idb files require IDA Pro (commercial, not installed here) to open; only the .asm text listing was used.
